title: Major Averages Slide More Firmly Into Negative Territory - U.S. Commentary
text:
Major Averages Slide More Firmly Into Negative Territory - U.S. Commentary April 19, 2018, 11:57:00 AM   Stocks have moved mostly lower over the course of the trading session on Thursday after seeing some early indecision. The major averages have slid firmly into negative territory after ending the previous session mixed. 
Currently, the major averages are just off their worst levels of the day. The Dow is down 90.20 points or 0.4 percent at 24,657.87, the Nasdaq is down 58.25 points or 0.8 percent at 7,236.98 and the S&P 500 is down 19.37 points or 0.7 percent at 2,689.27. 
A negative reaction to news from some well-known companies is contributing to the weakness on Wall Street in mid-day trading. 
Shares of Procter & Gamble (PG) have moved to the downside after the consumer products giant released its first quarter results a day earlier than expected. 
While P&G reported better than expected first quarter results, the company also announced it is buying the consumer health business of Germany's Merck for about $4.2 billion. 
Apple (AAPL) and Nvidia (NVDA) are also under pressure after key Asian chip partner Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) forecast weaker than expected second quarter revenues. 
On the other hand, shares of American Express (AXP) are moving significantly higher after the credit card giant reported first quarter results that beat analyst estimates on both the top and bottom lines. 
Aluminum producer Alcoa (AA) has also jumped after reporting better than expected first quarter earnings and raising its full-year guidance 
In U.S. economic news, the Labor Department released a report showing a modest decrease in first-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits in the week ended April 14th. 
The report said initial jobless claims edged down to 232,000, a decrease of 1,000 from the previous week's unrevised level of 233,000. Economists had expected jobless claims to dip to 230,000. 
A separate report released by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia showed regional manufacturing activity unexpectedly saw a modestly faster rate of growth in the month of April. 
The Philly Fed said its diffusion index for current general activity inched up to 23.2 in April from 22.3 in March, with a positive reading indicating growth in regional manufacturing activity. Economists had expected the index to dip to 20.1. 
Shortly after the start of trading, the Conference Board released a report showing its index of leading economic indicators increased in line with economist estimates in the month of March. 
The Conference Board said its leading economic index rose by 0.3 percent in March after climbing by an upwardly revised 0.7 percent in February. 
Sector News 
Tobacco stocks continue to see substantial weakness in mid-day trading, with the NYSE Arca Tobacco Index plunging by 5.5 percent. The index is extending the sharp pullback seen over the two previous sessions. 
Philip Morris (PM) is posting a particularly steep loss after reporting first quarter earnings that exceeded analyst estimates but on weaker than expected revenues. 
Significant weakness also remains visible among semiconductor stocks, as reflected by the 4.2 percent slump by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. The disappointing guidance by Taiwan Semiconductor is weighing on the sector. 
Housing stocks have also moved sharply lower over the course of the session, dragging the Philadelphia Housing Sector Index down by 3 percent. 
Computer hardware, telecom, and real estate stocks are also seeing considerable weakness on the day, while financial stocks have shown a strong move to the upside. 
Other Markets 
In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region continued to move to the upside during trading on Thursday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index edged up by 0.2 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped by 1.4 percent. 
Meanwhile, the major European markets turned in a mixed performance on the day. While the German DAX Index dipped by 0.2 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index and the French CAC 40 Index both rose by 0.2 percent. 
In the bond market, treasuries are extending the notable decline seen over the course of the previous session. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, is up by 6.1 basis points at 2.928 percent.
